rationale:
Split into 7 named lemmas. One is the comparator-accepted isoperimetric_apply_eq_zero_of_disjoint_support, reused with its identical frozen type.

The supplied proof of iwl_cr_cone_integer_multiplicity combines four unrelated techniques:
- test-form constructions on ℝ^{P+1} = ℝ × ℝ^P (Steps 2 and 5);
- support theory of the product current (Step 3);
- a calculus identity for the cone map h(y) = y_0·π(y) (Steps 4 and 6);
- a Fubini exchange on the representation X = τ(M, θ, ξ) (Step 8).

Each of these is a self-contained, reusable statement:
- slice_forms (Step 2): the slices η^♭_s of a test form are test forms, jointly continuous in (s, x).
- product_support (Step 3; uses slice_forms and vanish_off_support): let Z satisfy the interval-product formula over X, with spt X ⊆ B̄_R(0). Then spt Z lies in the compact set Φ([0,1] × B̄_R(0)). Its hypothesis is verbatim the conclusion of this node's dependency iwl_cr_interval_product_im.
- cutoff_pullback (Step 5): χ·f^#ω is a test form for C^∞ f and ω and a compactly supported C^∞ χ.
- product_cutoff (Step 5): ϑ(y_0)ζ(πy) is a C^∞ cut-off on ℝ^{P+1}.
- cone_map (Steps 4 and 6): h is C^∞, h(Φ(s,x)) = sx, and (α ∘ Dh(Φ(s,x)))(e_0, ιv) = s^m α(x, v).
- integral_exchange (Step 8): ∫_0^1 X(φ(s)) ds = X(ψ), for X integer multiplicity, φ jointly continuous and supported in a fixed compact K for s ∈ [0,1], and ψ the pointwise s-integral of φ.

The parent keeps the assembly: Steps 1, 4, 5, 7 and 9 as supplied, using its own resolved dependencies iwl_cr_interval_product_im and iwl_cr_radial_operator.
1. Obtain Z from iwl_cr_interval_product_im.
2. product_support gives a compact L ⊇ spt Z. Since spt Z = (zeroRegion)ᶜ is closed, h⁻¹(K) ∩ spt Z is compact for every compact K. cone_map gives h C^∞, so H_push yields an integer multiplicity S.
3. Fix ω. Let r := max(R, 0) + 1 and take ContDiffBump cut-offs ζ = 1 on B̄_r(0) and ϑ = 1 on [−1, 2]. Put χ := ϑ(y_0)ζ(πy) (product_cutoff) and η := χ·h^#ω (cutoff_pullback). Since χ = 1 on the open set N := {y_0 ∈ (−1, 2), ‖πy‖ < r} ⊇ L ⊇ spt Z, we get S(ω) = Z(η).
4. The slices φ of η (slice_forms) satisfy φ(s)(x)(v) = ζ(x)s^m ω(sx)(x, v) for s ∈ [0,1] (cone_map, with ϑ(s) = 1). Hence Z(η) = ∫_0^1 X(φ(s)) ds.
5. Let ψ_ω come from iwl_cr_radial_operator (k = a = m) and put ψ := ζψ_ω.
   - ψ is a test form satisfying the Hω-formula on B_r(0) ⊇ B̄_R(0) ⊇ spt X, so Cone(X, C) gives C(ω) = X(ψ).
   - tsupport φ(s) ⊆ tsupport ζ for s ∈ [0,1].
   - ψ(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 φ(s)(x)(v) ds.
6. integral_exchange with K := tsupport ζ gives ∫_0^1 X(φ(s)) ds = X(ψ). So S(ω) = C(ω) for every ω, hence S = C and C is integer multiplicity.

subproblems.title: Currents annihilate test forms supported off their support (reused accepted lemma)
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ, every set U ⊆ ℝ^P, every current T ∈ GeometricCurrentOn U n and every test form ω ∈ TestFormOn U n: if tsupport ω is disjoint from spt T = U ∖ zeroRegion(T), then T(ω) = 0. (Reuse, with identical frozen Lean type, of the comparator-accepted declaration isoperimetric_apply_eq_zero_of_disjoint_support.)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n), Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n)) T.support → T ω = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the accepted proof of the reused declaration isoperimetric_apply_eq_zero_of_disjoint_support (node root.isoperimetric-a1.vanish_off_support-a1), reproduced verbatim; the frozen Lean type is identical, so the comparator-accepted declaration is reused.

Notation. For T ∈ GeometricCurrentOn U n, `T.VanishesOn W` means T(η) = 0 for every η ∈ TestFormOn U n with tsupport η ⊆ W. Let 𝒲 be the family of all W ⊆ ℝ^P with W open, closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U and T.VanishesOn W. By definition T.zeroRegion = ⋃𝒲 and T.support = U ∖ T.zeroRegion.

1. Let K := tsupport ω. Since ω ∈ TestFormOn U n, ω is C^∞, has compact support (so K is compact, in particular closed) and K ⊆ U.
2. K ⊆ ⋃𝒲. Let x ∈ K. Then x ∈ U, and x ∉ T.support by the disjointness hypothesis, i.e. x ∉ U ∖ T.zeroRegion; hence x ∈ T.zeroRegion = ⋃𝒲.
3. Every member of 𝒲 is open, so by compactness of K there are finitely many W_1, …, W_r ∈ 𝒲 (r ≥ 0; r = 0 when K = ∅) with K ⊆ W_1 ∪ ⋯ ∪ W_r (e.g. `IsCompact.elim_finite_subcover_image`; it is convenient to index the cover by the resulting finite subfamily rather than by Fin r).
4. ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P), with the model with corners 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ^P), is a finite-dimensional, Hausdorff, σ-compact smooth manifold, and K is closed and covered by the open sets W_i (i ranging over the finite index set of step 3). Hence there is a smooth partition of unity on K subordinate to (W_i): C^∞ functions ψ_1, …, ψ_r : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with tsupport ψ_i ⊆ W_i for every i and Σ_i ψ_i(x) = 1 for every x ∈ K (Mathlib `SmoothPartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate`; a real-valued `ContMDiff 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ^P) 𝓘(ℝ)` function of class C^∞ is `ContDiff ℝ ∞` by `contMDiff_iff_contDiff`).
5. For each i put η_i(x) := ψ_i(x) • ω(x). Then η_i is C^∞ (a C^∞ scalar function times a C^∞ form). If ω(x) = 0 or ψ_i(x) = 0 then η_i(x) = 0, so support η_i ⊆ support ω ∩ support ψ_i; taking closures, tsupport η_i ⊆ K ∩ tsupport ψ_i ⊆ U ∩ W_i. In particular η_i has compact support (closed subset of the compact K). Thus η_i ∈ TestFormOn U n and tsupport η_i ⊆ W_i.
6. Since W_i ∈ 𝒲, T vanishes on W_i, so T(η_i) = 0 for every i.
7. ω = Σ_i η_i in TestFormOn U n (checked pointwise). If x ∈ K, then Σ_i ψ_i(x) • ω(x) = (Σ_i ψ_i(x)) • ω(x) = ω(x). If x ∉ K, then x ∉ support ω, so ω(x) = 0 and every η_i(x) = 0. (If r = 0 then K = ∅, ω = 0 and both sides are 0.)
8. T acts ℝ-linearly on TestFormOn U n (T.toCurrent is a linear map), so by steps 6 and 7, T(ω) = Σ_i T(η_i) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: tsupport ω is a compact subset of U disjoint from spt T, hence contained in the zero region, i.e. covered by the open sets W on which T vanishes.
Extract a finite subcover W_1, …, W_r of tsupport ω.
Take a smooth partition of unity ψ_1, …, ψ_r on tsupport ω subordinate to the W_i (Mathlib SmoothPartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate).
Each ψ_i • ω is a test form in U with tsupport in W_i, so T(ψ_i • ω) = 0.
ω = Σ_i ψ_i • ω pointwise, so T(ω) = 0 by linearity.

subproblems.title: Hyperplane slices of a test form on ℝ^{P+1} are test forms on ℝ^P, jointly continuous in the slice parameter
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ and η ∈ D^{m+1}(ℝ^{P+1}). Then there is a family φ : ℝ → D^m(ℝ^P) such that (s, x) ↦ φ(s)(x) is continuous from ℝ × ℝ^P to the m-covectors on ℝ^P, and φ(s)(x)(v) = η(Φ(s, x))(e_0, ι(v_1), …, ι(v_m)) for all s ∈ ℝ, x ∈ ℝ^P and v ∈ (ℝ^P)^m. Here Φ(s, x) = (s, x_1, …, x_P) = (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ x)), e_0 = EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 and ι(w) = Φ(0, w).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (η : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl (P + 1))) (m + 1)), ∃ φ : ℝ → TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) m, Continuous (fun p : ℝ × Eucl P => (φ p.1 : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) m) p.2) ∧ ∀ (s : ℝ) (x : Eucl P) (v : Fin m → Eucl P), (φ s : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) m) x v = (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl (P + 1)) (m + 1)) ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ x))) (Fin.cons (EuclideanSpace.single 0 1) fun i => (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons 0 (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ (v i))))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 2 (Slices) of the parent proof, filled in; compare SimonGMT `pointSlice_isTestForm` (Chapter06/Product.lean), the same argument for E × F.

Notation (used throughout): E := ℝ^P = Eucl P and E′ := ℝ^{P+1} = Eucl (P + 1), with the Euclidean norms; Φ(s, x) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ x)) ∈ E′ for s ∈ ℝ, x ∈ E, so Φ(s, x)_0 = s and Φ(s, x)_{j+1} = x_j (j ∈ Fin P); e_0 := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 ∈ E′; ι(w) := Φ(0, w) for w ∈ E; π(y) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ y)) ∈ E for y ∈ E′, so π(y)_j = y_{j+1}; y_0 := y 0 (= y.ofLp 0). D^k(E) := TestFormOn univ k (C^∞ k-forms with compact tsupport), D_k(E) := GeometricCurrentOn univ k; C^∞ means ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞), i.e. smooth of every finite order.

1. (ι and Φ.) ι(w)_0 = 0 and ι(w)_{j+1} = w_j, so ι is ℝ-linear (check coordinatewise), hence a continuous linear map ι : E →L[ℝ] E′ (every linear map between finite-dimensional spaces is continuous; alternatively build it from the coordinate maps). Comparing coordinates, Φ(s, x) = s • e_0 + ι(x) (coordinate 0: s·1 + 0 = s; coordinate j+1: s·0 + x_j = x_j). By EuclideanSpace.norm_eq and Fin.sum_univ_succ, ‖Φ(s, x)‖² = s² + Σ_j x_j² = s² + ‖x‖², so ‖x‖ ≤ ‖Φ(s, x)‖.
2. (The slice map on covectors.) For an (m+1)-covector α on E′ (α : Covector E′ (m + 1)) put ℒ(α) := (α.curryLeft e_0).compContinuousLinearMap ι, an m-covector on E. By ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft_apply_apply (Matrix.vecCons is Fin.cons), ℒ(α)(v) = α(Fin.cons e_0 (fun i => ι(v i))) for every v : Fin m → E. The map ℒ is continuous linear in α: it is the composite of the linear isometry ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeftLI, evaluation at e_0 (a continuous linear map on E′ →L[ℝ] Covector E′ m), and ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMapCLM ι. In particular ℒ(0) = 0 and ℒ is C^∞.
3. (Definition.) For s ∈ ℝ let φ_s : E → Covector E m, φ_s(x) := ℒ(η(Φ(s, x))). By step 2, φ_s(x)(v) = η(Φ(s, x))(Fin.cons e_0 (fun i => ι(v i))) for all x, v, which is the required formula.
4. (Smoothness.) x ↦ Φ(s, x) = s • e_0 + ι(x) is affine, hence C^∞; η is C^∞ because it is a test form; ℒ is C^∞ (step 2). Hence φ_s = ℒ ∘ η ∘ Φ(s, ·) is C^∞ (ContDiff.comp).
5. (Compact support.) Let A_s := {x ∈ E : Φ(s, x) ∈ tsupport η}. It is closed, as the preimage of the closed set tsupport η under the continuous map Φ(s, ·). If x ∉ A_s then η(Φ(s, x)) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport), so φ_s(x) = ℒ(0) = 0. Thus support φ_s ⊆ A_s, and tsupport φ_s ⊆ A_s (closure_minimal). Since tsupport η is compact it lies in some closed ball B̄_ρ(0) ⊆ E′; for x ∈ A_s, ‖x‖ ≤ ‖Φ(s, x)‖ ≤ ρ by step 1. So A_s ⊆ B̄_ρ(0) ⊆ E, which is compact (E is a proper space), and tsupport φ_s, a closed subset of it, is compact. (Equivalently: Φ(s, ·) is an isometry, hence a closed embedding, and A_s is compact by IsClosedEmbedding.isCompact_preimage.) Trivially tsupport φ_s ⊆ univ. Hence φ_s ∈ D^m(E) = TestFormOn univ m; define φ(s) := φ_s.
6. (Joint continuity.) (s, x) ↦ Φ(s, x) is continuous on ℝ × E (its coordinates are s and the x_j, composed with the continuous linear equivalence (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ).symm). η is continuous and ℒ is continuous. Hence (s, x) ↦ φ(s)(x) = ℒ(η(Φ(s, x))) is continuous on ℝ × E.
7. Steps 3, 5 and 6 show that φ has all the required properties. ∎
proof_key_steps: ℒ(α) := (α.curryLeft e_0).compContinuousLinearMap ι is a continuous linear map from (m+1)-covectors on ℝ^{P+1} to m-covectors on ℝ^P with ℒ(α)(v) = α(e_0, ι v_1, …, ι v_m).
φ(s) := ℒ ∘ η ∘ Φ(s, ·) is C^∞, being a composite of C^∞ maps (Φ(s, ·) = s e_0 + ι is affine).
tsupport φ(s) ⊆ Φ(s, ·)⁻¹(tsupport η), which is compact because ‖x‖ ≤ ‖Φ(s, x)‖.
(s, x) ↦ ℒ(η(Φ(s, x))) is continuous.

subproblems.title: The support of the product current [[(0,1)]] × X lies in the compact set Φ([0,1] × B̄_R(0))
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, R ∈ ℝ, X ∈ D_m(ℝ^P) with spt X ⊆ B̄_R(0), and Z ∈ D_{m+1}(ℝ^{P+1}) such that Z(η) = ∫_0^1 X(φ(s)) ds whenever η ∈ D^{m+1}(ℝ^{P+1}), φ : ℝ → D^m(ℝ^P) and φ(s)(x)(v) = η(Φ(s, x))(e_0, ι(v_1), …, ι(v_m)) for all s ∈ [0, 1], x ∈ ℝ^P, v ∈ (ℝ^P)^m (Φ, e_0, ι as in slice_forms). Then L := Φ([0, 1] × B̄_R(0)) = {Φ(p.1, p.2) : p ∈ [0, 1] × B̄_R(0)} is compact and spt Z ⊆ L.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (R : ℝ) (X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) m) (Z : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl (P + 1))) (m + 1)), X.support ⊆ closedBall 0 R → (∀ (η : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl (P + 1))) (m + 1)) (φ : ℝ → TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) m), (∀ s ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ∀ (x : Eucl P) (v : Fin m → Eucl P), (φ s : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) m) x v = (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl (P + 1)) (m + 1)) ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ x))) (Fin.cons (EuclideanSpace.single 0 1) fun i => (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons 0 (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ (v i))))) → Z η = ∫ s in (0 : ℝ)..1, X (φ s)) → IsCompact ((fun p : ℝ × Eucl P => (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons p.1 (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ p.2))) '' (Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 ×ˢ closedBall (0 : Eucl P) R)) ∧ Z.support ⊆ ((fun p : ℝ × Eucl P => (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons p.1 (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ p.2))) '' (Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 ×ˢ closedBall (0 : Eucl P) R))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 3 (Support of Z) of the parent proof, filled in, with B̄_R(0) in place of B̄_{R₀}(0) (if R < 0 the ball is empty and the same argument applies).

Notation (used throughout): E := ℝ^P = Eucl P and E′ := ℝ^{P+1} = Eucl (P + 1), with the Euclidean norms; Φ(s, x) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ x)) ∈ E′ for s ∈ ℝ, x ∈ E, so Φ(s, x)_0 = s and Φ(s, x)_{j+1} = x_j (j ∈ Fin P); e_0 := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 ∈ E′; ι(w) := Φ(0, w) for w ∈ E; π(y) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ y)) ∈ E for y ∈ E′, so π(y)_j = y_{j+1}; y_0 := y 0 (= y.ofLp 0). D^k(E) := TestFormOn univ k (C^∞ k-forms with compact tsupport), D_k(E) := GeometricCurrentOn univ k; C^∞ means ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞), i.e. smooth of every finite order. Let L := {Φ(p.1, p.2) : p ∈ [0, 1] × B̄_R(0)}, and call the hypothesis on Z (Prod).

1. (L is compact and closed.) [0, 1] is compact and B̄_R(0) ⊆ ℝ^P is compact (ℝ^P is proper; the ball is empty when R < 0), so [0, 1] × B̄_R(0) is compact (IsCompact.prod). The map p ↦ Φ(p.1, p.2) is continuous on ℝ × ℝ^P (its coordinates are p.1 and the coordinates of p.2, composed with the continuous linear equivalences EuclideanSpace.equiv). Hence L is compact (IsCompact.image), and closed because ℝ^{P+1} is Hausdorff.
2. (Forms supported off L are annihilated.) Let η ∈ D^{m+1}(ℝ^{P+1}) with tsupport η ∩ L = ∅. By slice_forms there is φ : ℝ → D^m(ℝ^P) with φ(s)(x)(v) = η(Φ(s, x))(Fin.cons e_0 (fun i => ι(v i))) for all s, x, v, in particular for s ∈ [0, 1]; so (Prod) gives Z(η) = ∫_0^1 X(φ(s)) ds. Fix s ∈ [0, 1] and let N_s := {x ∈ ℝ^P : Φ(s, x) ∉ tsupport η}. N_s is open: it is the preimage of the open complement of the closed set tsupport η under the continuous map x ↦ Φ(s, x).
   (a) B̄_R(0) ⊆ N_s: if ‖x‖ ≤ R then Φ(s, x) ∈ L, so Φ(s, x) ∉ tsupport η.
   (b) φ(s) vanishes on N_s: for x ∈ N_s, η(Φ(s, x)) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport), so φ(s)(x)(v) = 0 for every v, i.e. φ(s)(x) = 0. Hence support φ(s) ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ N_s, a closed set, and tsupport φ(s) ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ N_s (closure_minimal).
   (c) spt X ⊆ B̄_R(0) ⊆ N_s by hypothesis and (a), so tsupport φ(s) is disjoint from spt X by (b). By vanish_off_support (U := univ, T := X, ω := φ(s)), X(φ(s)) = 0.
   Thus s ↦ X(φ(s)) vanishes on [0, 1] = uIcc 0 1, so ∫_0^1 X(φ(s)) ds = ∫_0^1 0 ds = 0 (intervalIntegral.integral_congr), and Z(η) = 0.
3. (spt Z ⊆ L.) Let p ∈ ℝ^{P+1} with p ∉ L. Since L is closed, its complement is open and there is ε > 0 with B_ε(p) ∩ L = ∅ (Metric.isOpen_iff). Let W := B_{ε/2}(p). Then W is open; closure W = B̄_{ε/2}(p) (closure_ball, ε/2 ≠ 0) is compact and contained in univ; and closure W ⊆ B_ε(p) is disjoint from L. Z vanishes on W: if η ∈ D^{m+1}(ℝ^{P+1}) has tsupport η ⊆ W ⊆ closure W, then tsupport η ∩ L = ∅ and Z(η) = 0 by step 2. Hence W belongs to the family {W open : closure W compact, closure W ⊆ univ, Z vanishes on W} whose union is Z.zeroRegion, so p ∈ W ⊆ Z.zeroRegion and p ∉ Z.support = univ ∖ Z.zeroRegion.
4. Steps 1 and 3 give IsCompact L and Z.support ⊆ L. ∎
proof_key_steps: L = Φ([0,1] × B̄_R(0)) is compact (continuous image of a compact set) and closed.

If tsupport η misses L, each slice φ(s), s ∈ [0,1], from slice_forms vanishes on the open set N_s = {x : Φ(s,x) ∉ tsupport η} ⊇ B̄_R(0) ⊇ spt X, so X(φ(s)) = 0 by vanish_off_support and Z(η) = ∫_0^1 X(φ(s)) ds = 0.
Each p ∉ L has a ball B_{ε/2}(p) whose compact closure misses L; Z vanishes on it, so p lies in the zero region and p ∉ spt Z.

subproblems.title: A compactly supported cut-off of the pull-back of a smooth form by a smooth map is a test form
subproblems.statement: Let P, Q, k ∈ ℕ, f : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q a C^∞ map, χ : ℝ^P → ℝ a C^∞ function with compact support, and ω a C^∞ k-form on ℝ^Q (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl Q) k). Then there is η ∈ D^k(ℝ^P) = TestFormOn univ k with η(y) = χ(y) · (ω(f(y))).compContinuousLinearMap (Df(y)) for every y ∈ ℝ^P.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P Q k : ℕ) (f : Eucl P → Eucl Q) (χ : Eucl P → ℝ) (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl Q) k), ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) f → ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) χ → HasCompactSupport χ → ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) ω → ∃ η : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) k, ∀ y, (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) k) y = χ y • (ω (f y)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f y)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 5 (A good η) of the parent proof, first half (h^#ω is C^∞ and the cut-off has compact support), stated for an arbitrary C^∞ map f and cut-off χ; the parent applies it with f := h and χ(y) := ϑ(y_0) ζ(π y).

Notation: C^∞ means ContDiff ℝ ∞ with ∞ := ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞); p(y) := (ω(f y)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f y), a k-covector on ℝ^P.

1. (Df is C^∞.) f is C^∞ and ∞ + 1 ≤ ∞, so y ↦ fderiv ℝ f y is C^∞ (ContDiff.fderiv_right).
2. (ω ∘ f is C^∞.) ω and f are C^∞, so y ↦ ω(f y) is C^∞ (ContDiff.comp).
3. (The pull-back operator is C^∞.) Let 𝒫(B) := ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMapCLM B for B : ℝ^P →L[ℝ] ℝ^Q; it is the continuous linear map α ↦ α.compContinuousLinearMap B from k-covectors on ℝ^Q to k-covectors on ℝ^P. By ContinuousAlternatingMap.analyticOnNhd_compContinuousLinearMapCLM (with s := univ), 𝒫 is analytic on the whole space, hence C^∞ (AnalyticOnNhd.contDiff).
4. (p is C^∞.) p(y) = 𝒫(fderiv ℝ f y)(ω(f y)). By steps 1–3, y ↦ 𝒫(fderiv ℝ f y) is a C^∞ family of continuous linear maps and y ↦ ω(f y) is C^∞, so p is C^∞ (ContDiff.clm_apply).
5. (η is a test form.) Define η(y) := χ(y) • p(y). η is C^∞ (ContDiff.smul). χ has compact support, hence so does χ • p (HasCompactSupport.smul_right), and tsupport η ⊆ univ. So η satisfies IsTestForm (C^∞ and compact support) and lies in TestFormOn univ k.
6. By construction η(y) = χ(y) • (ω(f y)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f y) for every y. ∎
proof_key_steps: y ↦ Df(y) (ContDiff.fderiv_right) and y ↦ ω(f(y)) are C^∞.
B ↦ compContinuousLinearMapCLM B is analytic (Mathlib analyticOnNhd_compContinuousLinearMapCLM), hence C^∞, so p(y) = compContinuousLinearMapCLM (Df y) (ω(f y)) is C^∞ (ContDiff.clm_apply).
χ • p is C^∞ with compact support inherited from χ, hence a test form on univ with the stated values.

subproblems.title: The cone map h(y) = y_0 · π(y): smoothness, values on Φ(s, x), and its pull-back on (e_0, ιv)
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ and h : ℝ^{P+1} → ℝ^P, h(y) := y_0 · π(y) with π(y) = (y_1, …, y_P) = (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ y)). Then h is C^∞, and for all s ∈ ℝ, x ∈ ℝ^P: h(Φ(s, x)) = s x, and for every (m+1)-covector α on ℝ^P and every v ∈ (ℝ^P)^m, (α ∘ Dh(Φ(s, x)))(e_0, ι(v_1), …, ι(v_m)) = s^m α(x, v_1, …, v_m), where (α ∘ L) := α.compContinuousLinearMap L and Φ, e_0, ι are as in slice_forms.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ), ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) (fun y : Eucl (P + 1) => y 0 • (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ y))) ∧ ∀ (s : ℝ) (x : Eucl P), (fun y : Eucl (P + 1) => y 0 • (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ y))) ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ x))) = s • x ∧ ∀ (α : Covector (Eucl P) (m + 1)) (v : Fin m → Eucl P), (α.compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ (fun y : Eucl (P + 1) => y 0 • (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ y))) ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ x))))) (Fin.cons (EuclideanSpace.single 0 1) fun i => (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons 0 (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ (v i)))) = s ^ m * α (Fin.cons x v)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 4 and 6 of the parent proof (h(Φ(s, x)) = s x is C^∞; Dh(Φ(s, x))(Φ(σ, w)) = σ x + s w, so Dh(Φ(s, x)) e_0 = x and Dh(Φ(s, x))(ι v) = s v; multilinearity), filled in.

Notation (used throughout): E := ℝ^P = Eucl P and E′ := ℝ^{P+1} = Eucl (P + 1), with the Euclidean norms; Φ(s, x) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ x)) ∈ E′ for s ∈ ℝ, x ∈ E, so Φ(s, x)_0 = s and Φ(s, x)_{j+1} = x_j (j ∈ Fin P); e_0 := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 ∈ E′; ι(w) := Φ(0, w) for w ∈ E; π(y) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ y)) ∈ E for y ∈ E′, so π(y)_j = y_{j+1}; y_0 := y 0 (= y.ofLp 0). D^k(E) := TestFormOn univ k (C^∞ k-forms with compact tsupport), D_k(E) := GeometricCurrentOn univ k; C^∞ means ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞), i.e. smooth of every finite order. Let p_0(y) := y_0 and h(y) := p_0(y) • π(y).

1. (Linear pieces.) p_0 : ℝ^{P+1} → ℝ is a continuous linear functional (it is EuclideanSpace.proj 0). π is ℝ-linear, since π(y)_j = y_{j+1} coordinatewise, hence a continuous linear map π_L : ℝ^{P+1} →L[ℝ] ℝ^P (finite dimension; or explicitly the composite of the continuous linear equivalences EuclideanSpace.equiv with the continuous linear map w ↦ (j ↦ w (Fin.succ j)) = Fin.tail). So h(y) = p_0(y) • π_L(y).
2. (Smoothness.) Continuous linear maps are C^∞, so h = p_0 • π_L is C^∞ (ContDiff.smul).
3. (Values on Φ.) Φ(s, x)_0 = (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ x)) 0 = s, and π(Φ(s, x)) = (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ x))) = (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ x) = x (ContinuousLinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply, Fin.tail_cons, ContinuousLinearEquiv.symm_apply_apply). Hence h(Φ(s, x)) = s • x.
4. (Derivative.) p_0 and π_L have derivatives p_0 and π_L at every point. By the product rule for scalar times vector (HasFDerivAt.smul), h has derivative D_y := p_0(y) • π_L + p_0.smulRight (π_L y) at y, so fderiv ℝ h y w = y_0 • π(w) + w_0 • π(y) for all w ∈ ℝ^{P+1}. Take y := Φ(s, x); by step 3, y_0 = s and π(y) = x.
   • e_0 = EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 has (e_0)_0 = 1 and π(e_0) = 0 (all its coordinates j + 1 vanish), so D_y e_0 = s • 0 + 1 • x = x.
   • ι(v) = Φ(0, v) has ι(v)_0 = 0 and π(ι(v)) = v (step 3 with s = 0), so D_y(ι v) = s • v + 0 • x = s • v.
5. (Pull-back identity.) Let α be an (m+1)-covector on ℝ^P and v : Fin m → ℝ^P. Then (α.compContinuousLinearMap D_y)(Fin.cons e_0 (fun i => ι(v i))) = α(D_y ∘ Fin.cons e_0 (fun i => ι(v i))) = α(Fin.cons (D_y e_0) (fun i => D_y(ι(v i)))) (Fin.comp_cons) = α(Fin.cons x (fun i => s • v i)) (step 4). With c := Fin.cons (1 : ℝ) (fun _ : Fin m => s) : Fin (m + 1) → ℝ we have Fin.cons x (fun i => s • v i) = (fun j => c j • Fin.cons x v j) (check j = 0 and j = Fin.succ i via Fin.cases), so ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_smul_univ gives α(Fin.cons x (fun i => s • v i)) = (∏_j c j) • α(Fin.cons x v) = (1 · s^m) α(Fin.cons x v) (Fin.prod_univ_succ; the product of the constant s over Fin m is s^m). Hence the left side equals s^m * α(Fin.cons x v). (For m = 0 both sides are α(Fin.cons x v), as s^0 = 1.)
6. Steps 2, 3 and 5 are the three asserted facts. ∎
proof_key_steps: y ↦ y_0 and π are continuous linear maps, so h = y_0 • π(y) is C^∞ and h(Φ(s,x)) = s x.
Product rule: Dh(y)(w) = y_0 π(w) + w_0 π(y); at y = Φ(s,x) this maps e_0 ↦ x and ι(v) ↦ s v.
Hence (α ∘ Dh(Φ(s,x)))(e_0, ιv) = α(x, s v_1, …, s v_m) = s^m α(x, v) by multilinearity (map_smul_univ).

subproblems.title: The product ϑ(y_0) ζ(π y) of cut-offs on ℝ and ℝ^P is a cut-off on ℝ^{P+1}
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, ϑ : ℝ → ℝ and ζ : ℝ^P → ℝ be C^∞ functions with compact support. Then χ : ℝ^{P+1} → ℝ, χ(y) := ϑ(y_0) · ζ(π(y)) with π(y) = (y_1, …, y_P) = (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ y)), is C^∞ and has compact support.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (ϑ : ℝ → ℝ) (ζ : Eucl P → ℝ), ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) ϑ → HasCompactSupport ϑ → ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) ζ → HasCompactSupport ζ → ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) (fun y : Eucl (P + 1) => ϑ (y 0) * ζ ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ y)))) ∧ HasCompactSupport (fun y : Eucl (P + 1) => ϑ (y 0) * ζ ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ y))))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 5 (A good η) of the parent proof, the claim that the scalar factor ϑ(y_0) ζ(π y) is C^∞ with tsupport inside Φ(tsupport ϑ × tsupport ζ), which is compact; filled in.

Notation (used throughout): E := ℝ^P = Eucl P and E′ := ℝ^{P+1} = Eucl (P + 1), with the Euclidean norms; Φ(s, x) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ x)) ∈ E′ for s ∈ ℝ, x ∈ E, so Φ(s, x)_0 = s and Φ(s, x)_{j+1} = x_j (j ∈ Fin P); e_0 := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 ∈ E′; ι(w) := Φ(0, w) for w ∈ E; π(y) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ y)) ∈ E for y ∈ E′, so π(y)_j = y_{j+1}; y_0 := y 0 (= y.ofLp 0). D^k(E) := TestFormOn univ k (C^∞ k-forms with compact tsupport), D_k(E) := GeometricCurrentOn univ k; C^∞ means ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞), i.e. smooth of every finite order.

1. (Smoothness.) y ↦ y_0 is a continuous linear functional (EuclideanSpace.proj 0), and π is a continuous linear map (π(y)_j = y_{j+1}; composite of the continuous linear equivalences EuclideanSpace.equiv with the continuous linear map Fin.tail). Both are C^∞, so y ↦ ϑ(y_0) and y ↦ ζ(π y) are C^∞ (ContDiff.comp), and so is their product χ (ContDiff.mul).
2. (Norm splitting.) For y ∈ ℝ^{P+1}, EuclideanSpace.norm_eq and Fin.sum_univ_succ give ‖y‖² = Σ_{i : Fin (P+1)} y_i² = y_0² + Σ_{j : Fin P} y_{j+1}² = |y_0|² + ‖π(y)‖². Hence ‖y‖ ≤ |y_0| + ‖π(y)‖ (since √(a² + b²) ≤ a + b for a, b ≥ 0).
3. (Compact support.) tsupport ϑ and tsupport ζ are compact, hence bounded: there are a, b ≥ 0 with |t| ≤ a for all t ∈ tsupport ϑ and ‖z‖ ≤ b for all z ∈ tsupport ζ. If χ(y) ≠ 0, then ϑ(y_0) ≠ 0 and ζ(π y) ≠ 0, so y_0 ∈ support ϑ ⊆ tsupport ϑ and π(y) ∈ tsupport ζ, whence |y_0| ≤ a, ‖π(y)‖ ≤ b and ‖y‖ ≤ a + b by step 2. Thus support χ ⊆ B̄_{a+b}(0); this ball is closed, so tsupport χ ⊆ B̄_{a+b}(0) (closure_minimal), and it is compact (ℝ^{P+1} is proper). Hence tsupport χ is compact, i.e. HasCompactSupport χ (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset). ∎
proof_key_steps: y ↦ y_0 and π are continuous linear, so χ = (ϑ ∘ y_0) · (ζ ∘ π) is C^∞.
χ(y) ≠ 0 forces |y_0| ≤ a and ‖π y‖ ≤ b (bounds of the compact supports), so tsupport χ ⊆ B̄_{a+b}(0) is compact.

subproblems.title: An integer multiplicity current commutes with ∫_0^1 ds on a continuous, uniformly supported family of test forms
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, X ∈ D_m(ℝ^P) integer multiplicity, K ⊆ ℝ^P compact, φ : ℝ → D^m(ℝ^P) such that (s, x) ↦ φ(s)(x) is continuous on ℝ × ℝ^P and tsupport φ(s) ⊆ K for every s ∈ [0, 1], and ψ ∈ D^m(ℝ^P) with ψ(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 φ(s)(x)(v) ds for all x ∈ ℝ^P and v ∈ (ℝ^P)^m. Then ∫_0^1 X(φ(s)) ds = X(ψ).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) m) (K : Set (Eucl P)) (φ : ℝ → TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) m) (ψ : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) m), IsIntegerMultiplicity X → IsCompact K → Continuous (fun p : ℝ × Eucl P => (φ p.1 : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) m) p.2) → (∀ s ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, tsupport (φ s : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) m) ⊆ K) → (∀ (x : Eucl P) (v : Fin m → Eucl P), (ψ : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) m) x v = ∫ s in (0 : ℝ)..1, (φ s : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) m) x v) → ∫ s in (0 : ℝ)..1, X (φ s) = X ψ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 8 (Exchange of X and ∫ ds) of the parent proof: Fubini on the representation X = τ(M, θ, ξ), with the slice family abstracted to any jointly continuous, uniformly supported family φ and ψ its pointwise s-integral; filled in.

Notation: E := ℝ^P = Eucl P; μ := μHE[m] (the Hausdorff measure H^m on E); ν := volume.restrict (Ioc 0 1) on ℝ, a finite measure; an m-vector w ∈ NVector E m = (Covector E m →L[ℝ] ℝ) acts on an m-covector α by w(α).

1. (Representation.) As X is integer multiplicity there are M, θ, ξ with IsRectifiableTriple univ m M θ ξ, θ(x) ∈ ℕ for x ∈ M, and X(ω) = ∫_{x ∈ M} θ(x) ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ for every ω ∈ D^m(E) (tauAction). For x ∈ M, θ(x) > 0 (field pos) and θ(x) = k ∈ ℕ, hence θ(x) ≥ 1.
2. (A finite measure.) K is compact, hence closed and measurable, and K ⊆ univ, so θ is μ-integrable on M ∩ K (field integrableOn). M ∩ K is μ-null-measurable (field nullMeasurableSet), so μ.restrict (M ∩ K)-a.e. x lies in M ∩ K (ae_restrict_mem₀) and satisfies 1 ≤ θ(x). Therefore μ(M ∩ K) = ∫⁻_{M∩K} 1 dμ ≤ ∫⁻_{M∩K} ofReal(θ) dμ ≤ ∫⁻_{M∩K} ‖θ‖ₑ dμ < ∞, the last bound because θ is integrable on M ∩ K (HasFiniteIntegral). Let μ_K := μ.restrict (M ∩ K): a finite measure, for which θ is integrable and θ ≥ 1 a.e., and for which ξ is AEStronglyMeasurable (restrict the field aestronglyMeasurable from μ.restrict M to the smaller set; AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_measure, Measure.restrict_mono).
3. (Vanishing off K.) For s ∈ [0, 1] and x ∉ K we have x ∉ tsupport φ(s), so φ(s)(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport). For x ∉ K and any v, ψ(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 φ(s)(x)(v) ds = 0, because the integrand vanishes for s ∈ uIcc 0 1 = [0, 1] (intervalIntegral.integral_congr); hence ψ(x) = 0. Consequently, for s ∈ [0, 1], x ↦ θ(x) ξ(x)(φ(s)(x)) coincides with its product with the indicator of K, and so does x ↦ θ(x) ξ(x)(ψ(x)). By setIntegral_indicator (K measurable): X(φ(s)) = ∫ θ(x) ξ(x)(φ(s)(x)) dμ_K(x) for s ∈ [0, 1], and X(ψ) = ∫ θ(x) ξ(x)(ψ(x)) dμ_K(x).
4. (Uniform bound.) The continuous map (s, x) ↦ φ(s)(x) is bounded in norm on the compact set [0, 1] × K: there is B ≥ 0 with ‖φ(s)(x)‖ ≤ B for s ∈ [0, 1], x ∈ K (IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn); by step 3 the bound holds for all x ∈ E when s ∈ [0, 1]. By the field orients, for μ.restrict M-a.e. x (hence μ_K-a.e. x) there is an orthonormal τ : Fin m → E with ξ(x) = simpleNVector τ or ξ(x) = −simpleNVector τ; then for every m-covector α, |ξ(x)(α)| = |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖ ∏_i ‖τ_i‖ = ‖α‖ (simpleNVector_apply, ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm, ‖τ_i‖ = 1). Together with θ ≥ 0 μ_K-a.e. (step 2): for every s ∈ [0, 1] and μ_K-a.e. x, |θ(x) ξ(x)(φ(s)(x))| ≤ B θ(x).
5. (Integrability on the product.) Let F(s, x) := θ(x) ξ(x)(φ(s)(x)) on ℝ × E, with the measure ν.prod μ_K (both factors finite, hence s-finite).
   (a) F is AEStronglyMeasurable: (s, x) ↦ θ(x) and (s, x) ↦ ξ(x) are AEStronglyMeasurable for ν.prod μ_K (AEStronglyMeasurable.snd); (s, x) ↦ φ(s)(x) is continuous (Continuous.aestronglyMeasurable); the evaluation (w, α) ↦ w(α) is continuous (bilinear), so (s, x) ↦ ξ(x)(φ(s)(x)) is AEStronglyMeasurable (Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable₂), and so is the product F.
   (b) G(s, x) := B · θ(x) is ν.prod μ_K-integrable: the constant B is ν-integrable (ν finite) and θ is μ_K-integrable, so Integrable.mul_prod applies.
   (c) |F| ≤ G holds ν.prod μ_K-a.e.: ν-a.e. s lies in Ioc 0 1 ⊆ [0, 1] (ae_restrict_mem), the bound of step 4 holds for μ_K-a.e. x, and since Prod.fst and Prod.snd are quasi-measure-preserving (Measure.quasiMeasurePreserving_fst/snd) both statements hold ν.prod μ_K-a.e.
   Hence F is ν.prod μ_K-integrable (Integrable.mono').
6. (Fubini.) By MeasureTheory.integral_integral_swap applied to F: ∫ (∫ F(s, x) dμ_K(x)) dν(s) = ∫ (∫ F(s, x) dν(s)) dμ_K(x).
7. (Left side.) For s ∈ Ioc 0 1 ⊆ [0, 1], ∫ F(s, x) dμ_K(x) = X(φ(s)) by step 3. Hence the left side of step 6 is ∫_{Ioc 0 1} X(φ(s)) ds (setIntegral_congr_fun on the measurable set Ioc 0 1), which is ∫_0^1 X(φ(s)) ds (intervalIntegral.integral_of_le, as 0 ≤ 1).
8. (Inner integral of the right side.) Fix x ∈ E. The map s ↦ φ(s)(x) is continuous, hence bounded on [0, 1] and ν-integrable. For each v : Fin m → E, evaluation α ↦ α(v) is a continuous linear functional on m-covectors (e.g. ContinuousMultilinearMap.apply composed with ContinuousAlternatingMap.toContinuousMultilinearMapCLM), so by ContinuousLinearMap.integral_comp_comm, (∫ φ(s)(x) dν(s))(v) = ∫ φ(s)(x)(v) dν(s) = ∫_0^1 φ(s)(x)(v) ds = ψ(x)(v); hence ∫ φ(s)(x) dν(s) = ψ(x) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.ext).
